plan.title: Labs 7/9/10 Windows install fails with npm.cmd EINVAL instead of the documented not-learner-ready stop

narratives.Description: Labs 7/9/10 Windows install fails with npm.cmd EINVAL instead of the documented not-learner-ready stop
narratives.Overview:
## What happened

Labs 7, 9, and 10 document native Windows/PowerShell as a candidate, not learner-ready. Their helpers also contain assert.notEqual(process.platform, "win32", "Native Windows/PowerShell is a candidate path and is not learner-ready in this release.").

On this Windows host, create succeeded for all three under %TEMP%\3ci-directive-lab0{7,9,10}-*/repo. install then failed before the documented stop:

Lab 7 stopped: spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.cmd EINVAL
Lab 9 stopped: spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.cmd EINVAL
Lab 10 stopped: spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.cmd EINVAL

Node v26.8.1, npm 11.19.0. createIsolatedTools never ran, so the learner never sees "not learner-ready." The capstone helper already avoids this by invoking process.execPath plus npm-cli.js on win32.

## Why this is hard for a human

The lab text says "Use a dedicated zsh terminal." There is no Windows paste path. A mid-level engineer who reasonably adapts node <helper> create gets a Node EINVAL on npm.cmd under C:\Program Files\nodejs\ (space in path / .cmd without shell:true). That looks like a broken fixture, not an intentional environment block. Recovery tables do not mention EINVAL.

Practical outcomes for Modules 7, 9, and 10 are environment-blocked on this Windows host. Capstone (which has a real Windows path) completed.

## Suggested repair

Fail create on win32 with the existing not-learner-ready message, or reuse the capstone runNpm pattern and ship a PowerShell path, or put a boxed Windows stop before any create command. Do not leave create succeeding and install dying with EINVAL.
